local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 every Wyoming county elects its clerk, treasurer, assessor, coroner, sheriff, clerk of district court and county attorney or district attorney for four years, and the county commissioners whose terms are up, all with parties on the ballot; school district and community college trustees are elected the same day without parties. Cities and towns elect mayors and council members that day too, unless a town has chosen by charter ordinance to vote in May, and each special district (conservation, fire, hospital, cemetery and others) elects its directors in March, May or November as the district has decided, so not every district is on this ballot. Circuit and district judges and Supreme Court justices do not run against anyone: voters are asked whether to keep them.
local_calendar.s: W.S. 22-2-105 (county offices and judges), 22-22-102 (school and college trustees), 22-23-202 (towns that vote in May), 22-29-112 (special districts), 22-6-117 and 22-6-125 (which offices carry parties)

local_coverage.t: Wyoming has no statewide list of local candidates: each county clerk publishes its own. Loaded here: 521 county, city, school and special district contests with 1034 candidates in 17 of the 23 counties, read from the county clerks' November sample ballots (Sweetwater, Albany, Park, Teton, Uinta, Carbon, Converse, Goshen, Sublette, Platte, Crook, Hot Springs and Johnson), the clerks' candidate rosters (Laramie, Natrona and Big Horn) and, for school, college and special district offices only, the clerk's list of filings (Fremont); 18 of the contests have no candidate on their list. The 21 judges standing for retention come from the Secretary of State's own file. Left out: ballot questions and constitutional amendments, and the 6 counties named among the gaps, whose clerks had posted their sample ballots as scanned pictures, or no November sample ballot and only a list this loader does not read yet; in Fremont County the county's own offices and the cities' are among the gaps too. A school or special district that crosses a county line is shown once, with every county whose ballots carry it. Names rotate from precinct to precinct, so no ballot order is given; a candidate who withdrew is simply not printed on a ballot and cannot be counted there.
local_coverage.s: County clerks' 2026 general election sample ballots and rosters; Wyoming Secretary of State, 2026 General Election Candidates; W.S. 22-6-122 (names rotated)
